record_identity.title: Material risk assessment omits alternate access routes to the same capability

summary: A material risk is identified for an AI capability and a safeguard is prescribed or deployed on one access surface, but the applicable risk or impact assessment does not include materially relevant alternate routes to the same or equivalent capability. The omitted route can therefore remain outside the intended control boundary even though the underlying hazardous capability and risk condition are unchanged.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Risk attaches to capability, exposure and foreseeable effect rather than merely to the name of an interface. A production, research, evaluation, contractor, vendor, feedback, internal or delegated access route can expose materially equivalent capability while receiving different safeguards. Where the difference was not identified and justified through the applicable risk assessment, local control coverage can create false system-level assurance.

source_records.deployment_context: Contractors evaluating Anthropic models through systems used to collect human-feedback data.
source_records.source_context: Anthropic reports that from May 2025 until April 2026 all traffic through its systems for collecting human-feedback data from contractors ran without blocking biological classifiers. The affected pool was roughly 50,000 people and around 133 million exchanges. Anthropic reports that it fully remediated the issue and found no evidence of concerning chemical or biological misuse, while noting that discovery of this gap increased its concern that similar unknown coverage issues could exist.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary evidence of materially different safeguard coverage across an alternate access route to model capability for which biological risk controls had already been deployed. The public report establishes the coverage gap but does not expose every internal risk-assessment artefact, so the precise organisational root cause remains bounded.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: direct public retrieval of the official Anthropic risk report text
limitations: The public report does not disclose all internal risk registers, architecture diagrams, control-assignment records or vendor configurations.
The report states that Anthropic found no evidence of concerning chemical or biological misuse from the affected traffic.
The assessment-scope interpretation is a VIGIL governance inference from the disclosed safeguard-coverage gap and is not represented as Anthropic's own root-cause finding.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Relied on for the duration, scale, access pathway, missing biological classifier coverage, remediation status and stated absence of concerning misuse. VIGIL separately classifies the upstream governance mechanism as failure to carry an identified material risk across the full relevant access boundary.

contextual_relations.rationale: FM-0053 applies where a required monitoring boundary omits a material surface or can be circumvented. FM-0066 is upstream and broader: the applicable risk or impact assessment fails to include a materially relevant access route to the hazardous capability, whether the missing control is monitoring, a blocking classifier, an access restriction, an approval gate or another safeguard.

FM-0054 concerns declared evaluation conditions diverging from operative reality. FM-0066 concerns incomplete risk-assessment scope across alternate access surfaces even where each surface's local technical state is accurately represented.

FM-0056 concerns technical reachability being mistaken for permission. FM-0066 concerns failure to carry an already identified risk and its control requirements across materially relevant routes to the same capability.

failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which an organisation or governed AI system identifies a material risk associated with a capability, model, tool or effect, but the applicable risk or impact assessment, system-boundary model, risk register, control assignment or assurance process fails to enumerate and evaluate one or more materially relevant alternate access routes by which actors can reach the same or materially equivalent capability. A safeguard can therefore be present on one route and absent or materially weaker on another without an explicit, justified and independently reviewable difference in risk treatment. The defining failure is incomplete risk-boundary analysis across access surfaces, not merely a classifier false negative, a known in-scope control deployment bug, a monitoring miss or unauthorised downstream action.
failure_threshold: The threshold is met where: (1) a material risk has been identified for a capability, model, tool or effect; (2) at least one safeguard, restriction, monitoring obligation or other control is prescribed or deployed in response; (3) another materially relevant access route reaches the same or materially equivalent capability or effect; and (4) that route is omitted from, inadequately represented in, or unjustifiably excluded from the applicable risk or impact assessment such that the prescribed control does not apply, applies materially differently without documented justification, or is not independently verified. A known in-scope route on which a required control simply fails to deploy may additionally constitute implementation failure; an omitted monitoring route may additionally constitute FM-0053.

harm_vectors: known hazardous capability exposed through an unassessed route
silent safeguard variance by access surface
contractor or vendor pathway outside the effective risk boundary
false system-level assurance from local control coverage
failure_classification.severity_assessment_basis: S1 reflects a demonstrated safeguard-coverage gap affecting a biological-risk control across approximately 133 million exchanges and roughly 50,000 contractor accounts over about eleven months. Anthropic reports no concerning chemical or biological misuse, so catastrophic realised harm is not established; the mechanism nevertheless concerns a high-consequence capability for which blocking safeguards had already been judged necessary.
failure_classification.likelihood: demonstrated in the Anthropic contractor pathway; recurrence is plausible wherever risk assessment and safeguard assignment are organised by interface, team, vendor or deployment surface rather than by capability and exposure
failure_classification.confidence: high for the disclosed incident and safeguard-coverage gap; moderate for the precise internal root cause because complete internal assessment artefacts are not public
failure_classification.failure_scope: cross-surface risk assessment, model-access architecture, third-party and contractor pathways, frontier AI
failure_classification.recurrence_pattern: May recur when assessments inventory the primary product surface but fail to model contractor, vendor, research, evaluation, post-training, internal, delegated or substitute routes to materially equivalent capability.
failure_classification.taxonomy_reference: CAM-EQ2026-OPERATIONS-003-SUP-01 Appendix B — OPS.FF.GOVERNANCE family; no explicit alternate-access-route risk-assessment subtype identified in the current operational taxonomy as reviewed on 2026-08-22
failure_classification.persistence: Persists until materially relevant access surfaces are enumerated and mapped to the underlying capability and risk, differences in control treatment are explicitly justified, and assurance verifies actual coverage.
failure_classification.reproducibility: Testable through authorised architecture and risk-register review that enumerates actors, interfaces, credentials, contractor and vendor routes, research and evaluation pathways, post-training systems, internal tools and substitute channels, then compares the applicable risk classification and control set for materially equivalent capability exposure.
failure_classification.visibility: Often low because each access surface may appear locally valid while only cross-surface comparison of risk registers, architecture, controls and telemetry reveals that the identified risk is not consistently governed.

cam_internal.governance_layer: impact and risk assessment scope, system-boundary and access-surface modelling, safeguard assignment and cross-surface assurance
cam_internal.routing_note: Primary diagnostic classification is governance because the identified material risk was not carried across the full relevant access boundary. SECURITY is substantively implicated because it owns system and deployment boundary, interface, permission and security-risk doctrine. OPERATIONS is implicated through governance-reach, assurance, audit and the operational failure taxonomy. LATTICE-001/002/003 govern civilian-lattice integrity, access denial and conflict-condition continuity respectively and are not presently treated as source-authoritative owners of generic model-access topology.
cam_internal.validator_or_automation_impact: No immediate schema change required. A subsequent taxonomy cross-reference transformation should ensure every FM resolves to an explicit operational failure-taxonomy class or an expressly provisional mapping.

ecosystem_status.basis: Anthropic reports that the identified contractor-pathway gap has been remediated, but explicitly states that discovering the gap increases its concern about other similar unknown issues. The general mechanism remains applicable to multi-surface AI development and deployment architectures.
